solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cream drunk with coffee's filling

indicators.note: something drunk is reeling and disordered, so these letters are jumbled
the filling of a word is its inside, everything but its outer letters

parts.note: the word coffee, with 's read as is; its filling is everything inside its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes their coffee with cream, perhaps a drinker's order at a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like what goes in the drink but is the colour; 'drunk' is the signal to jumble, not a description of anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream is a pale yellowish shade close to white, so it is an example of that colour family.

clue.text: Dance floor — let it be firm!

parts.note: amen means so be it, let it be
CO, short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A dancer insists the floor should be solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is a passionate Spanish style of dance from Andalusia.

clue.text: Base, centre for ironworks, was heaving

indicators.note: centre for picks out the middle letter of the word

parts.note: the middle letter of ironworks
retched means was heaving, gagging

explanation.surface: A sickly worker at the middle of a steel plant was throwing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low and contemptible; wretched has the same despicable sense.

clue.text: Keen on local couple getting a hearing

indicators.note: getting a hearing means listened to, so the sound counts

parts.note: in (at the local pub) plus two (a couple)

explanation.surface: Two people at the pub are listened to sympathetically.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a neighbourhood pub, so being at the local is being IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Into is informal for enthusiastic about something, as in being into jazz.

clue.text: Six slices no use, having turned green?

indicators.note: the six cuts into the other piece, inside it
turned over and reordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Six portions of something are no good once they have gone mouldy and green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having turned' looks like food going off, matching 'green', but it signals the rearrangement of 'no use'.
explanation.definitionFit: Green with envy is the idiom, so green means jealous or covetous.

clue.text: What a jury looks for out of hearing?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: blocking noise, so not audible

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words it is reliable evidence; as one word it describes an insulated room.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundproof room keeps noise from passing through; a jury wants sound, solid evidence.

clue.text: Authors with another set of neat procedures?

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a cow
rites are set ceremonial procedures

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a fresh set of tidy methods.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat here is the old noun for cattle, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-write is to compose jointly with a partner, so authors with another.

clue.text: Catches heartless politician's alternative take on past

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter

parts.note: to catch is to hear
a Tory, a Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A cynical politician catches out others with a revisionist view of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle A of HEARS to give HERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Herstory is feminist history told from women's perspective, a rewriting of the conventional record.

clue.text: Hope one's somehow done with book — the novel I detest

indicators.note: done somehow, any old way, so these letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: the word one, with 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader tries to sort out a scrambled message before finishing a book they dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but the definition is the remark of someone who dislikes anything new.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophobe has a fear or dislike of anything new, so would say they detest novelty.

clue.text: From puzzle Learner to Victor: congratulations!

parts.note: a maze is a puzzle of paths
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solver progresses from novice to winner and is cheered.
explanation.definitionFit: Mazel tov is a Hebrew and Yiddish expression of good wishes, used like well done.

clue.text: Courts controversy, ultimately displaying guts all round

indicators.note: the guts go all the way round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: innards are guts, the internal organs

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of controversy

parts.note: last letter of controversy

explanation.surface: Law courts are embroiled in a dispute, with someone's nerve on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' is not law courts but enclosed yards. 'Guts' is the innards, not courage.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn yard is the open enclosed space of an inn, a courtyard, so the plural means courts.

clue.text: Engaged in campaigning, as bail is set

definitions.meaning: first meaning: out making political speeches, canvassing for votes
second meaning: in cricket the bails rest on top of the stumps

explanation.walkthrough: 'bail' suggests release from custody; here it is a cricket bail, a small crosspiece resting on the stumps (the three upright sticks of the wicket).
explanation.definitionFit: Campaigning politicians once spoke standing on tree stumps, giving the idiom; a cricket bail sits literally on the stump tops.

clue.text: Matches used when building is in flames?

indicators.note: building means constructing anew, so these letters are assembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Matches were struck when a building caught fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' looks like the things that light fires but means sporting fixtures; 'building' is a verb working on IS IN FLAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Semifinals are the contests deciding who reaches the final, so they are sporting matches.

clue.text: Oil rings going around on the water?

indicators.note: the two rings go around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: each O looks like a ring
on the water means teetotal, abbreviated TT

explanation.surface: Oil slicks form rings that spread across water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the water' is not afloat but drinking only water, i.e. teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a variant of attar, a fragrant essential oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Ad hoc term for recent coalition government? Name to censure

parts.words: Ad hoc term for recent coalition government
parts.note: Con-Dem was the nickname for the 2010-15 British coalition of Conservatives and Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: A journalist's invented label for a government is used to criticise it.
explanation.walkthrough: The UK's 2010 coalition of Conservatives (Con) and Liberal Democrats (Dem) was dubbed the ConDems by critics.
explanation.definitionFit: To condemn is to express strong disapproval, a close synonym of censure.

clue.text: Holding it together after upset is what fellow's about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fellow goes around the other piece

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a fellow, with 's read as is

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns these letters upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: eh? means what?

explanation.surface: Someone keeps calm after a shock, which is what a man is all about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IS + EH to HESI, and COVE (an old British word for a chap) goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesive describes something that sticks together and forms a united whole.

clue.text: Seed — not a bean from France — that's primary source of sustenance

parts.note: a nut is a seed
rien is French for nothing, not a bean

indicators.note: primary means first, so the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of that's

explanation.surface: A seed lacking a French bean is a basic food source.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a bean is an idiom for nothing at all; the French is rien.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance providing nourishment, essential for life and growth.

clue.text: Target to raise before retiring

parts.note: to cock is to raise, as a dog cocks its ears
retiring means shy, reserved

explanation.surface: A shy person is set up as a target before withdrawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockshy is a fairground stall where things are thrown at a target, hence any object of attack.

clue.text: Cockney's shed tears to stun old bounder

indicators.note: tears means rips apart, so one piece splits the other and sits inside it

parts.note: KO, knockout, is to stun

indicators.note: a Cockney drops his aitches, so the H goes

parts.note: a hangar is a large shed for aircraft

explanation.surface: A Cockney cries and stuns an aged cad.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, from East London, drops the initial H, so HANGAR becomes ANGAR; it 'tears' KO apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo moves by leaping, so it bounds; the clue plays on bounder as a cad.

clue.text: Parties of Americans do extensive gardening job in SE England?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lively American folk-dance gatherings

definitions.text: do extensive gardening job in SE England?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: hoe the Downs, the chalk hills of south-east England

explanation.walkthrough: The North and South Downs are ranges of chalk hills in south-east England; weeding them all would be a big task.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a country dance party in the US, especially with square dancing.

clue.text: Where you'll find LA: North Dakota? Not true!

parts.note: in the sol-fa scale la comes just before te, so it is pre-te
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: A disbelieving query about where Los Angeles is located.
explanation.walkthrough: LA looks like Los Angeles, but it is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale (do re mi fa so la te), coming before TE.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, pretend means make-believe or fake, so not real.

clue.text: African having quit ought to return at intervals

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so these letters are read in the opposite order
at intervals takes every other letter of the words

parts.note: the words quit ought, read backwards then taken every other letter

explanation.surface: An African should come back now and then after leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every second letter of 'quit ought' gives UTUH; 'return' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are a Bantu-speaking people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a member is an African.

clue.text: Foreign ref upset one pointing to the spot?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An overseas referee, annoyed, points to the penalty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture of a referee pointing to the penalty spot is a decoy; the definition is the index finger.
explanation.definitionFit: The forefinger is the index finger, the one used for pointing at a place or a mark.

clue.text: Knock the beer back: easily one's undoing?

indicators.note: back means reversed, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: tonk is slang for to hit hard
pils is short for pilsner, a pale lager

explanation.surface: Downing a beer quickly could be a drinker's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock the beer back' looks like drinking; 'back' instead reverses TONK and PILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipknot is a knot designed to come undone with a pull, so it is easily untied.

clue.text: Some work by British composer

parts.note: an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A piece written by an English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places the B beside ERG, before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School, who wrote Wozzeck.

clue.text: Couple quizzically raised one's casually viewing broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out loud, so we go by the sound

parts.note: I browse: one is looking through casually

explanation.surface: Two people raise questions while one idly watches a television broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' is not two people but a pair of features raised in surprise or doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebrows come in a pair and are lifted when someone is puzzled or questioning.

clue.text: Physicist's brief fussily interrupting archdeacon

definitions.note: the physicist is, with 's read as is

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of another piece

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

indicators.note: brief means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: anally means fussily, in an over-fastidious way

explanation.surface: A scientist's fussy short report interrupts a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon in the Church of England is addressed as the Venerable, abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: James Van Allen was the American scientist after whom Earth's radiation belts are named.

clue.text: Disgrace to follow: put up with that

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
to house is to put up, accommodate

explanation.surface: Someone disgraced is told to go along with it and tolerate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doghouse is an idiom for being in disfavour or disgrace.
